questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute requires corporations located in the state to pay an annual property tax based on the value of their inventory that is stored there. A tire distributor that imports tires manufactured in foreign countries and stores them at warehouses located in the state has sued to challenge the state tax, arguing that it is unconstitutional.
Is the state tax constitutional?

choices.A: No, because the import-export clause prohibits state taxes on imported goods.
choices.B: No, because the state tax discriminates against foreign commerce.
choices.C: Yes, because states have absolute authority to tax goods within their borders.
choices.D: Yes, because the state tax does not divert import revenue from the federal government.

questions.explanation:
State taxation of imported goods
Federal government can speak with one voice
(federal government can tax goods during import process)
+
Interstate harmony not disturbed
(Complete Auto test)
  • Substantial nexus between state & taxed person/activity
  • Fairly apportioned pursuant to rational formula
  • Not discriminatory against interstate commerce
  • Fairly related to state services/benefits
+
Import revenue not diverted from federal government
(state tax applies after goods are imported)
=
Tax complies with
state import-export clause

The import-export clause generally prohibits state taxation of imported goods unless Congress consents or the tax is absolutely necessary for the state to execute its inspection laws. Additionally, a state tax on imported goods is valid if:

  • the federal government is still able to spea k with one voice in foreign commerce
  • there is interstate harmony because the tax satisfies the Complete Auto requirements and
  • the tax does not divert import revenue from the federal government.

Here, the state tax does not impair the federal government's ability to speak with one voice because the tax applies after the goods have gone through the import process. This means that the federal government may still tax the goods as they are imported. The tax also does not disturb interstate harmony because it:

  • applies to inventory that is stored at the distributor's warehouses in the state (substantial nexus)
  • is based on a rational formula that only taxes the value of the inventory in the state (fairly apportioned)
  • applies equally to imported and domestic goods (nondiscriminatory) (Choice B) and
  • is reasonable compared to services and benefits provided by the state (fairly related).

Therefore, the tax does not divert import revenue from the federal government since the tax applies after the goods have been imported. It merely compensates the state for goods stored in the state. Therefore, the state tax is constitutional (Choice A).

(Choice C) The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states any power that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government, including the power to generally tax goods within their borders. But this power is not absolute because states must comply with other constitutional provisions (eg, the import-export clause).

📌 Educational Objective

A state tax on imported goods is valid if (1) the federal government is still able to speak with one voice in foreign commerce, (2) there is interstate harmony because the tax satisfies the Complete Auto requirements, and (3) the tax does not divert import revenue from the federal government.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. 1, § 10, cl. 2 (state import-export clause).
  • Itel Containers Int'l Corp. v. Huddleston, 507 U.S. 60, 76–78 (1993) (setting forth the components of the modern import-export clause test).
  • 71 Am. Jur. 2d State and Local Taxation § 74 (explaining when a state tax violates the import-export clause).
questions.zh-question:
某州法规要求，位于该州的公司须根据其储存在该州的库存价值缴纳年度财产税。一家进口外国制造轮胎并将其储存在该州仓库的轮胎分销商提起诉讼，对该州税收提出质疑，主张其违宪。

该州税收是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为《进出口条款》(import-export clause) 禁止州对进口商品征税。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为该州税收歧视了对外贸易。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为各州拥有对其境内商品征税的绝对权力。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为该州税收并未分流本应属于联邦政府的进口税收收入。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：进出口条款与州税收权
核心考点：进出口条款 (Import-Export Clause)

美国宪法第一条第10款第2项规定：未经国会同意，任何州不得对进出口货物征收“关税” (Imposts or Duties)。

现代测试标准 (Modern Test)

根据最高法院在 Michelin Tire Corp. v. Wages (1976) 案中的裁决，并非所有针对进口商品的税收都被禁止。只有属于“关税”性质的税收才被禁止。

判断州税是否违宪，需看其是否违反以下三个政策目标：

  1. 联邦统一发声 (One Voice)： 是否干扰联邦政府在对外关系中的统一立场？
  2. 联邦收入 (Federal Revenue)： 是否分流了本应属于联邦政府的进口关税收入？
  3. 州际和谐 (Interstate Harmony)： 是否破坏州际贸易和谐（例如对过境商品征税）？
本案分析逻辑
1
税收性质： 这是一个非歧视性的从价财产税 (Nondiscriminatory Ad Valorem Property Tax)。它针对的是州内所有企业的库存，而不仅仅是进口商品。
2
征税时机： 轮胎已经存放在该州的仓库中，处于“静止”状态，享受该州提供的公共服务（如警察、消防、道路）。
3
是否分流联邦收入？ 没有。该税收是对州内财产价值的征税，用于支付州服务的成本，而不是对“进口行为”本身征税。因此，它没有夺走联邦政府的关税收入。
✅ 正确答案：D

合宪，因为该州税收并未分流本应属于联邦政府的进口税收收入。

这是 Michelin 测试的三个分支之一。只要该税收是非歧视性的财产税，且针对的是已经停止运输并储存在州内的货物，它就不被视为宪法禁止的“关税” (Impost or Duty)。

为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 A (原包装原则)： 错误。旧的“原包装原则” (Original Package Doctrine) 认为只要货物还在原包装内就免税，但这一原则已被推翻。现在即使在原包装内，只要货物在该州有了实质性停留，就可以被征收非歧视性财产税。
选项 B (歧视)： 错误。题目明确指出该法规要求“位于该州的公司”纳税，并未针对外国商品进行特殊征税。相反，如果免除进口商品的税收，反而会歧视国内商品。
选项 C (绝对权力)： 错误。在宪法题中，看到“绝对权力” (Absolute Authority) 几乎总是错的。州的征税权受到《进出口条款》和《商业条款》 (Commerce Clause) 的限制。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
当看到“非歧视性从价财产税” (Nondiscriminatory Ad Valorem Property Tax) 作用于进口商品时：
  • 如果商品正在运输途中 (In Transit) ➡️ 州不能征税。
  • 如果商品已经到达目的地并储存 (Came to rest) ➡️ 州可以征税。
本题中轮胎已经存储在仓库，故可以征税。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Due to the high cost of labor, several large corporations shut down their manufacturing plants in a state and moved their operations overseas. This caused severe and continuous unemployment in the state, which relies heavily on manufacturing jobs and manufactured goods to spur its economy. In response, the state legislature enacted a statute that requires certain businesses selling goods in the state to purchase goods produced in the state in an amount equal to at least half of the business's annual sales in the state. This statute only applies to businesses with annual sales in the state that exceed $3 million.
A company that has annual sales in the state of $5 million challenges the state statute in federal court.
Which constitutional provision provides the strongest ground on which to attack this statute?

choices.A: The Article I commerce clause.
choices.B: The Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.
choices.C: The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause.
choices.D: The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause.

questions.explanation:
Dormant commerce clause
(state regulation of interstate commerce)
Type of regulation Examples Standard
Discriminatory
(favors in-state interests)
  • Taxing out-of-state products more heavily
  • Requiring use of in-state products/services
 Unconstitutional unless:
  • furthers legitimate state interest and
  • no reasonable alternative
Nondiscriminatory
(otherwise burdensome)
  • Prohibiting all commercial vehicles on state highways
  • Overly strict requirements for all commercial shipments
 Unconstitutional if:
  • burden clearly exceeds local benefits

The Article I commerce clause gives Congress extensive authority to regulate interstate commerce. This clause also carries a negative implication (ie, the dormant commerce clause), which prohibits states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. Discrimination against interstate commerce—ie, favoring in-state over out-of-state economic interests—is unconstitutional unless (1) it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and (2) no reasonable alternative exists.

Here, the state statute discriminates against interstate commerce since it requires certain businesses to purchase substantial goods in the state at the expense of out-of-state competitors. The statute was enacted to relieve severe and continuous unemployment in the state. But since that interest is economic in nature, it cannot justify discrimination against interstate commerce. Therefore, the commerce clause is the strongest constitutional basis on which to attack this statute.

(Choice B) Under the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause, state laws that substantially impact a fundamental right are almost always found invalid under strict scrutiny. But since there is no fundamental right to engage in business, a due process challenge would likely fail.

(Choice C) Discriminatory state laws that substantially impact a fundamental right or protected class generally violate the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. But since no fundamental right is implicated and businesses are not a protected class, the statute likely satisfies this clause.

(Choice D) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause prohibits states from infringing on the very limited rights of national citizenship—none of which are at issue here.

📌 Educational Objective

State laws that favor in-state over out-of-state economic interests violate the dormant commerce clause unless (1) they further a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and (2) no reasonable alternative exists.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).
  • Maine v. Taylor, 477 U.S. 131, 138 (1986) (explaining that the appropriate test for a dormant commerce clause challenge depends on whether the burden on interstate commerce is discriminatory or nondiscriminatory).

一家在该州年销售额为500万美元的公司，在联邦法院对该州法规提出质疑。

哪一项宪法条款为攻击此项法规提供了最有力的依据？

zh-choices.A: Article I 的商业条款。
zh-choices.B: 第十四修正案的正当程序条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations
正确答案：A (Commerce Clause)

本题考察的核心是休眠商业条款 (Dormant Commerce Clause, DCC)。这是MBE宪法部分非常高频的考点。

核心法律规则 虽然宪法 Article I 赋予国会管理州际商业的权力，但最高法院推导出该条款具有“消极”或“休眠”的一面：禁止各州通过歧视或过度负担州际商业的法律。

1. 判题逻辑：歧视性 vs. 非歧视性

在分析DCC问题时，首先要判断州法律是否对州外利益构成歧视 (Discrimination)。

类型 定义 审查标准
歧视性法规
(Discriminatory)		 偏袒州内经济利益，打压州外竞争者（如本题）。 几乎总是违宪 (Per se invalid)。
除非：
1. 目的为非经济的合法利益；
2. 无其他替代方案。
非歧视性法规
(Nondiscriminatory)		 对州内和州外企业一视同仁，但客观上阻碍了商业流通。 Pike 平衡测试：
只有当负担明显超过本地收益时才违宪。

2. 本案分析

  • 事实认定：该州法律要求企业购买“本州生产”的商品（Buy Local）。
  • 性质：这是典型的表面歧视 (Facial Discrimination)。它直接偏袒本州制造业，排斥外州商品。
  • 例外测试：
    • 州政府的目的是解决失业问题。虽然解决失业是好事，但在DCC分析中，这属于经济保护主义 (Economic Protectionism)。
    • 关键点：最高法院明确规定，经济利益不能作为歧视州际商业的正当理由。

因此，该法律违反了 Article I 的商业条款。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 B、C、D 都涉及第十四修正案 (14th Amendment)。对于一般的商业/经济法规（不涉及基本权利或受保护阶层）：

  • Due Process & Equal Protection: 仅适用合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)。只要法律与合法的政府利益（如减少失业）有合理关联即可通过。该州法律很可能通过此测试，因此这两条不是攻击法律的“最有力”依据。
  • Privileges or Immunities: 该条款在历史上被最高法院（Slaughter-House Cases）解释得非常狭窄，仅保护极少数的“国民权利”（如跨州迁徙权），几乎从不用于推翻商业法规。
💡 考场实战技巧
当题目中出现“州法律” (State Statute) 且该法律偏袒本地企业 (Favoring local business) 或 限制外州商品 (Restricting out-of-state goods) 时：
  1. 首先考虑 Dormant Commerce Clause。
  2. 如果目的是“保护本地经济”（如本题的就业），该法律必死无疑（违宪）。
  3. 如果目的是“健康或安全”（如禁止进口某种带病害的鱼），则可能幸存，但需证明没有其他替代手段。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Widgets are manufactured wholly from raw materials mined and processed in a state. The only two manufacturers of widgets in the United States are also located in that state. However, their widgets are purchased by retailers located in every state.
The state legislature is considering the adoption of a statute that would impose a tax solely on the manufacture of widgets. The tax is to be calculated at 3% of their wholesale value.
Which of the following arguments would be LEAST helpful to the state in defending the constitutionality of this proposed state tax on widgets?

choices.A: A tax on the manufacture of widgets may be imposed only by the state in which the manufacturing occurs and, therefore, it is not likely to create the danger of a multiple tax burden on interstate commerce.
choices.B: At the time widgets are manufactured and taxed they have not yet entered the channels of interstate commerce.
choices.C: Because of the powers reserved to them by the Tenth Amendment, states have plenary authority to construct their tax system in any manner they choose.
choices.D: The economic impact of this tax will be passed on to both in-state and out-of-state purchasers of widgets and, therefore, the tax is wholly nondiscriminatory in its effect.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
State taxation of interstate commerce (Complete Auto test)
State tax on interstate commerce valid if tax:
  • applied to person or activity with substantial nexus to state
  • fairly apportioned to avoid taxing interstate activities performed in other states
  • does not discriminate against interstate commerce AND
  • fairly related to services & benefits provided by state

Under the Tenth Amendment, any power that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government—including the power to construct a state tax system—is reserved to the states. But here, this is the least helpful argument for the state because this power is not plenary (ie, absolute). Instead, states must comply with other constitutional provisions. For example, a state tax on interstate commerce (as seen here) must comply with the dormant commerce clause and is only valid if it:

  • is applied to persons or activities with a substantial nexus to the state—eg, widgets manufactured from raw materials mined and processed in the state
  • is fairly apportioned to avoid taxing interstate activities performed in other states and thereby imposing multiple tax burdens—eg, tax imposed only in state where manufacturing occurs (Choice A), tax applied before widgets enter channels of interstate commerce (Choice B)
  • does not discriminate by favoring in-state over out-of-state entities—eg, economic impact passed on to both in-state and out-of-state purchasers (Choice D) and
  • is fairly related (ie, reasonable compared) to services and benefits provided by the state—eg, police protection, public roads.
📌 Educational Objective

Under the dormant commerce clause, states cannot tax interstate commerce unless the tax is (1) levied on persons or activities that have a substantial nexus with the state, (2) fairly apportioned, (3) nondiscriminatory, and (4) fairly related to state-provided services or benefits.

📚 References
  • Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady, 430 U.S. 274, 279 (1977) (setting forth the four-factor test used to determine if a state tax violates the commerce clause).
  • 71 Am. Jur. 2d State and Local Taxation § 157 (2019) (explaining how state taxation cannot unduly burden interstate commerce).

该州立法机构正在考虑通过一项法规，专门对小部件的制造征税。该税款将按其批发价值的3%计算。

在为这项拟议的州级小部件税的合宪性进行辩护时，以下哪项论点对该州最没有帮助？

zh-choices.A: 对小部件制造的征税只能由制造业所在的州进行，因此，这不太可能对州际贸易造成多重税收负担的风险。
zh-choices.B: 在小部件被制造和征税时，它们尚未进入州际贸易的渠道。
zh-choices.C: 由于Tenth Amendment赋予各州的保留权力，各州拥有以其选择的任何方式构建其税收制度的全权。
zh-choices.D: 此税的经济影响将转嫁给州内和州外的小部件购买者，因此，该税在其效果上是完全非歧视性的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations & Taxation
正确答案：选项 C

理由：第十修正案（10th Amendment）并不是各州违反宪法其他条款（如商业条款）的“挡箭牌”。

核心考点：休眠商业条款

本题考察的是休眠商业条款 (Dormant Commerce Clause) 对州政府征税权的限制。

虽然宪法没有明确禁止州对州际贸易征税，但最高法院通过判例确立了规则：如果国会没有立法，各州也不能通过歧视或过度负担的方式阻碍州际贸易。

Complete Auto 测试标准

根据 Complete Auto Transit v. Brady (1977) 案，一项针对州际贸易的州税必须满足以下四个条件才合宪：

  • 实质性联系 (Substantial Nexus)： 征税对象必须与该州有实质联系。
  • 公平分摊 (Fair Apportionment)： 税收必须根据在该州进行的活动比例进行分摊，避免多重征税。
  • 非歧视性 (Nondiscrimination)： 不得歧视州外商业。
  • 合理相关 (Fair Relationship)： 税收必须与州提供的服务（如警察、道路）合理相关。
为什么 C 选项最没有帮助？

题目要求选出最没有帮助 (LEAST helpful) 的辩护理由。

选项 C 声称：根据第十修正案，各州拥有构建其税收制度的“全权” (Plenary Authority)。

法律缺陷：这是一个致命的法律错误。虽然第十修正案保留了各州的权力，但这些权力受制于宪法（根据至高条款 Supremacy Clause）。

各州的征税权不是绝对的 (Not Plenary)。如果州税违反了商业条款（例如歧视州际贸易），那么无论第十修正案如何规定，该税都是违宪的。因此，声称拥有“绝对权力”在法庭上是无效的辩护。

为什么其他选项是有帮助的？

其他三个选项都在试图证明该税符合 Complete Auto 测试的要求：

  • 选项 A (公平分摊)： 强调制造只发生在一个州，因此不会有其他州对同一活动征税，避免了“多重税收负担”。这是在辩护该税符合 Fair Apportionment。
  • 选项 B (实质性联系/时机)： 强调征税发生在进入州际贸易渠道之前。这有助于证明该税是针对州内活动（制造）的，符合 Substantial Nexus，且历史上曾被视为不属于“商业”范畴（虽然现代观点已变，但这仍是一个支持州权的论点）。
  • 选项 D (非歧视性)： 强调税负由州内和州外购买者共同承担，证明该税没有歧视外州人。这是在辩护该税符合 Nondiscrimination。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

看到 "Plenary" (全权/绝对)、"Unlimited" (无限) 这样的词描述州权力时要高度警惕。在联邦宪法架构下，各州的权力极少是绝对的，通常都要受到联邦宪法（特别是商业条款和第十四修正案）的限制。

当题目问“最没有帮助的论点”时，通常是在寻找一个法律上错误的陈述，或者一个被判例法明确驳回的理论。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A federal statute requires all owners of mineral springs to pay a sales tax on the mineral water they sell. A state that sells mineral water from the springs that it owns has refused to pay the tax. The United States has sued the state in federal court, seeking payment of the tax. The state has moved to dismiss the action.
Is the court likely to dismiss the action?

choices.A: No, because Congress has unlimited power to tax and spend for the general welfare.
choices.B: No, because the nondiscriminatory tax does not interfere with the essential functions of state government.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment prohibits states from being sued in federal court without the state's consent.
choices.D: Yes, because the Tenth Amendment grants states immunity from all direct federal taxation.

questions.explanation:
Federalism
(power distribution between federal & state governments)
Constitutional provision Effect
Article VI supremacy clause
  • Prioritizes U.S. Constitution, treaties & federal laws over state constitutions & laws
  • Prohibits states from regulating/taxing federal government or its agencies/instrumentalities
Tenth Amendment
  • Reserves all powers not assigned to federal government by U.S. Constitution to states/people
  • Prohibits federal government from requiring states to enact laws or enforce federal laws
  • Immunizes states from federal taxes that discriminate against states or unduly interfere with essential state functions

Article I grants Congress the broad power to tax and spend for the general welfare. But this power is not unlimited (Choice A). Under the Tenth Amendment, Congress is prohibited from imposing federal taxes on states that:

  • discriminate against states because the taxes apply to states and their agencies but not private individuals or entities or
  • would unduly interfere with the states' essential functions, including property used for or income received from the state's performance of traditional government actions (eg, public schools, state parks).

However, the Tenth Amendment does not immunize states from nondiscriminatory federal taxes that apply to the public and private sectors and do not interfere with essential state functions (Choice D).

Here, the federal sales tax is nondiscriminatory since it applies to all private and public owners of mineral springs who sell mineral water. The tax also does not unduly interfere with essential state functions because selling mineral water (or any other product) is a business action—not a traditional government action. As a result, the Tenth Amendment does not immunize the state from the tax, so the court is not likely to dismiss the action.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state in federal court without the state's consent. However, this amendment does not bar actions brought by the United States (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The Tenth Amendment immunizes states from federal taxes that discriminate against states or unduly interfere with essential state functions.

📚 References
  • New York v. United States, 326 U.S. 572, 582 (1946) (holding that a state is not immune from a nondiscriminatory federal tax that does not interfere with essential state functions).
questions.zh-question:
一项联邦法规要求所有矿泉的所有者对其销售的矿泉水缴纳销售税。一个州份从其拥有的泉水中销售矿泉水，但拒绝缴纳该税。美国已在联邦法院起诉该州，要求其支付税款。该州已动议驳回此诉讼。

法院是否可能驳回此诉讼？

zh-choices.B: 不会，因为这项非歧视性税收不会干涉州政府的基本职能。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为 Eleventh Amendment 禁止在未经州份同意的情况下，在联邦法院起诉州份。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为 Tenth Amendment 授予州份豁免权，使其免于所有直接的联邦税收。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations (联邦与州的关系)
核心法律规则

Intergovernmental Tax Immunity (政府间税收豁免权)

联邦政府有权对州政府的活动征税，但必须满足两个条件：

  1. 非歧视性 (Nondiscriminatory)：税收必须同样适用于私营部门，不能仅针对州政府。
  2. 不干涉基本职能 (No Interference with Essential Functions)：税收不能不当干涉州的主权职能（如立法、执法、司法）。

如果州政府从事的是商业活动 (Proprietary/Business Activities)，而非传统的政府职能，且税收是非歧视性的，则州政府没有豁免权。

✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 B)

本题中，联邦税收针对的是所有矿泉水销售者（包括私人和公共所有者），因此它是非歧视性 (Nondiscriminatory) 的。

其次，销售矿泉水属于一种商业行为，并非州政府的“基本职能” (Essential Sovereign Function)。

结论： 既然税收是非歧视性的，且未干涉州的核心主权，联邦政府有权征收，法院不会驳回诉讼。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 A (过于绝对)：

虽然联邦征税权很广，但并非与对个人征税“完全相同”。第十修正案 (10th Amendment) 仍然保护州免受那些会“摧毁”其主权存在的税收。如果税收直接针对州的基本职能（如对州议会大楼征收房产税），则是违宪的。

选项 C (程序性陷阱)：

这是一个常见的 MBE 陷阱。第十一修正案 (11th Amendment) 确实禁止个人起诉州，但它不禁止联邦政府 (The United States) 起诉州。本案原告是美国政府，因此诉讼有效。

选项 D (误解豁免权范围)：

州并没有豁免于“所有”直接联邦税收。只要税收是非歧视性的且不破坏州的主权，州就必须像普通企业一样纳税。

💡 MBE 提分技巧

遇到“联邦向州征税”的题目，请按以下步骤思考：

  • 第一步： 该税是仅针对州（歧视性），还是针对所有人（普遍适用）？如果是普遍适用，通常是合宪的。
  • 第二步： 该活动是核心政府职能（如警察、立法），还是商业活动（如卖水、经营公园）？如果是商业活动，通常没有豁免权。
  • 第三步： 检查原告是谁。如果是 United States v. State，第十一修正案不适用。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state representative made a speech on the floor of the state legislature in which she asserted that a state senator had violated the legislature's code of ethics by having a sexual relationship with a staff member. In making this assertion, the representative played a recording of a phone conversation between the senator and staff member in which they admitted having such a relationship. The representative obtained the recording from an acquaintance, who had placed an illegal wiretap on the staff member's phone.
One year later, the federal government initiated a prosecution against the state representative for violating a federal criminal statute that prohibits the intentional publication of communications that were unlawfully recorded. A person found guilty under the statute is subject to a one-year prison sentence and a monetary fine.
The representative has moved to dismiss the action.
Is the court likely to dismiss the action?

choices.A: No.
choices.B: Yes, because state legislators are absolutely immune from liability for actions taken pursuant to their official legislative functions.
choices.C: Yes, because the Eleventh Amendment bars actions of this kind in federal court.
choices.D: Yes, because the speech or debate clause wholly insulates state legislators from civil and criminal liability for legislative activity.

questions.explanation:
State legislative immunity
Absolute immunity Legislative acts that are subject of:
  • state civil or criminal action
  • federal civil action
No immunity Legislative acts that are subject of:
  • federal criminal action

State legislators generally possess absolute immunity from state civil or criminal liability for actions taken pursuant to official legislative functions (eg, making speeches in the legislature).* In the context of federal civil and criminal liability, the Supreme Court has held that a state legislator's absolute immunity:

  • extends to federal civil liability because the federal government's interest in ensuring private civil actions is outweighed by the substantial impact such actions have on state legislative functions but
  • does not extend to federal criminal liability because the federal government's important interest in enforcing criminal statutes outweighs the minimal impact prosecutions have on state legislative functions.

As a result, the state representative is not immune from federal prosecution for violating the federal statute, and the court will likely not dismiss the action (Choice B).

*State legislative immunity derives from the common law. Today, most states have codified legislative immunity in their constitutions or statutes.

(Choice C) The Eleventh Amendment generally prohibits private parties and foreign governments from suing a state or state official for money damages in federal court. However, this amendment does not apply to actions initiated by another state or the United States (as seen here).

(Choice D) The speech or debate clause of the U.S. Constitution wholly insulates members of Congress, but not state legislators, from civil and criminal liability for any official legislative activity.

📌 Educational Objective

A state legislator has absolute immunity from federal civil liability for official legislative actions. However, this immunity does not extend to federal criminal liability.

📚 References
  • Tenney v. Brandhove, 341 U.S. 367, 378–79 (1951) (holding that state legislators are immune from civil liability for acts performed in the regular course of the legislative process).
  • United States v. Gillock, 445 U.S. 360, 373 (1980) (stating that a state legislator is subject to criminal prosecution for a violation of federal law).
  • 72 Am. Jur. 2d States, Territories, and Dependencies § 62 (2020) (explaining state legislative immunity).

一名州众议员在州立法机构的议事厅发表演讲，在演讲中，她声称一名州参议员与一名工作人员发生性关系，从而违反了立法机构的道德准则。在做出这一断言时，该众议员播放了一段参议员与该工作人员之间的电话通话录音，录音中他们承认了有此种关系。该众议员从一位熟人处获得了该录音，此人对该工作人员的电话进行了非法窃听。

一年后，联邦政府对该州众议员提起诉讼，指控其违反了一项联邦刑事法规，该法规禁止故意公布通过非法录音获取的通讯内容。根据该法规，被判有罪者将被处以一年监禁和罚款。

该众议员已动议驳回此项诉讼。

法院是否可能驳回此项诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不会。
zh-choices.B: 会，因为州立法者对其根据其官方立法职能所采取的行动享有绝对豁免权，可免于承担责任。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为 Eleventh Amendment 禁止在联邦法院进行此类诉讼。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为 speech or debate clause 完全使州立法者免于因立法活动而承担民事和刑事责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations / Constitutional Law
正确答案：A (No)
核心结论：法院不会驳回此案。虽然州立法者在履行立法职能时享有广泛的豁免权，但这种豁免权不适用于联邦刑事起诉。
⚖️ 法律依据与推理
本题考察的是州立法豁免权 (State Legislative Immunity) 的边界。我们需要区分两个维度：
  1. 主体：是联邦国会议员还是州议员？
  2. 责任类型：是民事责任 (Civil Liability) 还是刑事责任 (Criminal Liability)？
关键规则 (The Rule)：
根据联邦普通法，州立法者对其官方立法行为（如在议会发表演讲）享有免受联邦民事诉讼的绝对豁免权。

⚠️ 但是： 这种豁免权并不延伸至联邦刑事诉讼。
参见判例：United States v. Gillock (1980)
本案分析：
虽然该众议员的行为（在议会发表演讲）属于典型的立法活动，且如果这是一起民事诽谤诉讼，她将享有豁免权。但本案是联邦政府提起的刑事起诉（违反联邦窃听法规）。最高法院认为，联邦执行刑事法律的重大利益超过了保护州立法独立性的利益。因此，她不能免于受审。
📊 豁免权速记矩阵
诉讼类型 联邦国会议员
(Speech or Debate Clause)		 州立法者
(Common Law)
民事责任 ✅ 豁免 ✅ 豁免 (针对立法行为)
刑事责任 ✅ 豁免 (针对立法行为) ❌ 无豁免 (联邦刑事)
❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 B (Yes, absolute immunity...)：
错误。该选项混淆了民事和刑事豁免。虽然州立法者对立法行为享有绝对的民事豁免权，但如上所述，这不适用于联邦刑事起诉。
选项 C (Eleventh Amendment)：
错误。第十一修正案 (Eleventh Amendment) 禁止私人公民在联邦法院起诉州政府。但它不禁止联邦政府 (United States) 起诉一个州或州官员。本案原告是联邦政府。
选项 D (Speech or Debate Clause)：
错误。这是一个常见的陷阱。美国宪法中的 Speech or Debate Clause (Art. I, § 6) 仅适用于联邦国会议员，不适用于州立法者。州立法者的豁免权来自普通法，而非宪法此条款。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state owned and operated an electric power system, which included a nuclear power plant. In order to ensure the availability of sites for the disposal of spent fuel from the nuclear power plant, the state refused to supply electric power to out-of-state purchasers residing in states that would not accept spent fuel from the plant for storage or disposal.
Assume that no federal statute applies.
Which of the following is the strongest argument that the state's action is constitutional?

choices.A: A state may condition the sale to out-of-state purchasers of any products produced in that state on the willingness of those purchasers to bear their fair share of the environmental costs of producing those products.
choices.B: The generation of electricity is intrastate by nature and therefore subject to plenary state control.
choices.C: The state itself owns and operates the power system, and therefore its refusal to supply power to out-of-state purchasers is not subject to the negative implications of the commerce clause.
choices.D: The state's action is rationally related to the health, safety, and welfare of state citizens.

questions.explanation:
Dormant commerce clause analysis
State law favors in-state over
out-of-state economic interests
Yes
No
Discriminatory law

Strict scrutiny:

  • Law furthers legitimate
    interest and
  • no reasonable alternative
Nondiscriminatory law

Undue burden test:

  • Burden on commerce
    clearly exceeds local
    benefits
No
Yes
Other exceptions
  • Congressional authorization
  • State as market participant
  • Subsidy
  • Traditional government function
Yes
No
Constitutional
Unconstitutional

The commerce clause grants Congress extensive authority to regulate interstate commerce. And the negative implication of this clause (ie, the dormant commerce clause) prohibits states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. But states are not restrained by this clause when they participate in the market by, for example, buying or selling goods or services (ie, market-participant exception).

Here, the state discriminated against interstate commerce by refusing to supply electricity to out-of-state purchasers residing in states that would not store or dispose of spent fuel. But since the state itself owns and operates the power system, the market-participant exception applies. As a result, the state's refusal to supply power is not subject to the negative implications of the commerce clause. Therefore, this is the strongest argument that its action is constitutional.

(Choice A) Discrimination against interstate commerce may be justified if it furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and no reasonable alternative exists. But a state's economic interest in sharing the environmental costs of production with out-of-state purchasers cannot justify such discrimination.

(Choice B) Although generating electricity is intrastate (ie, within a state) by nature, supplying electricity to out-of-state purchasers is an interstate activity. But a state does not violate the dormant commerce clause by refusing to supply electricity to out-of-state purchasers when, as here, the state is acting as a market participant.

(Choice D) All powers not explicitly granted to the federal government by the Constitution are reserved to the states through the Tenth Amendment. This includes the states' police power to take action that is rationally related to protecting the health, safety, and welfare of its citizens. But this power does not allow states to violate other constitutional provisions—including the dormant commerce clause.

📌 Educational Objective

A state's activities are not restricted by the dormant commerce clause when the state is acting as a market participant (as opposed to a market regulator).

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8, cl. 3 (commerce clause).
  • Reeves, Inc. v. Stake, 447 U.S. 429, 439–40 (1980) (holding that a state is not subject to the dormant commerce clause when it acts as a market participant).
  • 15A Am. Jur. 2d Commerce § 33 (2019) (explaining the market-participant exception to the dormant commerce clause).
questions.zh-question:
一个州拥有并运营着一个电力系统，其中包括一座核电站。为了确保有可用的场址来处理核电站的乏燃料，该州拒绝向那些不愿接收该电站乏燃料进行储存或处置的州的州外购买者供电。

假设没有联邦法规适用。

以下哪项是支持该州行为合宪的最有力论据？

zh-choices.A: 一个州可以将在本州生产的任何产品销售给州外购买者的条件，设置为这些购买者愿意承担生产这些产品所产生的环境成本中的公平份额。
zh-choices.B: 发电本质上是州内行为，因此受到州的完全控制。
zh-choices.C: 该州自己拥有并运营该电力系统，因此其拒绝向州外购买者供电的行为不受《商业条款》消极含义的约束。
zh-choices.D: 该州的行为与州公民的健康、安全和福祉有合理关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law | Dormant Commerce Clause

核心考点：市场参与者例外 The Market Participant Exception
本题考察的是休眠商业条款 (Dormant Commerce Clause) 的一个重要例外。通常情况下，各州不得歧视州际商业或对其施加过度负担。
但是，当州政府不再是“监管者 (Regulator)”，而是作为“市场参与者 (Market Participant)”（即买方或卖方）进入市场时，它就不受休眠商业条款的约束。
为什么选 C 是正确的？
正确答案 C
分析：题目明确指出该州“拥有并运营 (owned and operated)”该电力系统。

这意味着该州在市场上销售电力，就像任何私人企业一样。根据市场参与者例外原则，该州有权选择它的交易对象（Trading Partners）。它可以决定只卖给本州居民，或者只卖给那些愿意接收核废料的州的居民。

因为该州是市场参与者，所以它拒绝向特定州外购买者供电的行为，完全豁免于休眠商业条款的限制。
相关判例参考：
Reeves, Inc. v. Stake (1980)
最高法院裁定，南达科他州拥有的水泥厂可以在水泥短缺期间优先向本州居民出售水泥，而拒绝向州外买家出售。法院认为，当州作为私营企业的经营者行事时，它享有与私营贸易商相同的选择交易对象的权利。
为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A 错误 试图用“环境成本公平份额”来辩护。如果州是作为监管者（Regulator）行事，这种基于经济利益的歧视通常是违宪的。只有“市场参与者例外”才能为这种明显的歧视提供强有力的宪法依据。
选项 B 错误 声称发电是“州内行为 (Intrastate)”。这是错误的法律结论。电力一旦进入电网跨境传输，就是典型的州际商业 (Interstate Commerce)。
选项 D 错误 声称这与“健康、安全和福祉 (Police Power)”有关。虽然州有警察权，但如果州作为监管者公然歧视州际商业（只卖给某些州，不卖给其他州），通常需要通过严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)，即证明该措施对于实现非经济的合法目的至关重要且没有替代方案。这是一个很难满足的标准。相比之下，选项 C 的“市场参与者例外”是一个绝对的抗辩理由，不需要进行复杂的利益平衡。
MBE 考试技巧
遇到涉及州政府歧视外州人的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：
  1. 第一步：看是否有联邦法律授权？（本题说 Assume no federal statute applies）。
  2. 第二步：看州政府的角色。
    • 如果是制定规则限制私人交易 ➡️ 适用休眠商业条款（通常违宪）。
    • 如果是自己买卖商品/服务 ➡️ 适用市场参与者例外（通常合宪）。
看到 "State owned and operated" 这种字眼，立刻联想 Market Participant Exception。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law requires any lawn mower sold in the state to meet a specified minimum level of fuel efficiency.
A new federal statute requires all power equipment, including lawn mowers, to be labeled with energy efficiency stickers to permit purchasers to make informed choices when buying such equipment. The statute does not expressly preempt state law.
Assume that no other federal statute or administrative regulation addresses the energy efficiency of power equipment.
Which of the following is the best argument the state can make for the continued validity of its law?

choices.A: Congress cannot preempt state laws requiring a specified minimum level of fuel efficiency for lawn mowers, because the use of such equipment is a wholly local event and, therefore, is beyond the regulatory authority vested in Congress by the commerce clause.
choices.B: The law is unaffected by the federal statute, because Congress did not expressly prohibit state laws requiring power equipment to meet specified levels of fuel efficiency.
choices.C: The purpose of the law is consistent with the purpose of the federal statute, enforcement of the law would not interfere with the full execution of the statute, and there is no evidence that Congress intended to preclude the states from enacting supplemental laws on this subject.
choices.D: There is a very strong presumption that a specific state law on a subject normally within the state's police power prevails over a more general federal statute, because the Tenth Amendment reserves to the states primary authority over matters affecting public health, welfare, and safety.

questions.explanation:
Doctrine of preemption

Federal law supersedes state & municipal laws by:
Express preemption
  • Constitution says federal regulation is exclusive
    OR
  • Federal law expressly prohibits state/municipal regulation
Implied preemption
Field preemption
  • Congress's pervasive regulation shows intent to occupy entire field
Conflict preemption
  • Direct - nearly impossible to comply with both laws
    OR
  • Indirect - state/municipal law frustrates federal law’s purpose

The Article VI supremacy clause allows a federal law to preempt a conflicting state law, thereby rendering the state law void and without effect. But there is a presumption against preemption—whether express or implied—that can only be overcome when Congress clearly intended to supersede the state law.

Here, the federal statute requiring power equipment (including lawn mowers) to have energy efficiency stickers does not expressly preempt the state law requiring lawn mowers to meet a minimum fuel-efficiency level. But the state must also show that the federal statute does not impliedly preempt the state law (Choice B). It can do so here because:

  • there is no evidence that Congress intended to fully occupy the field of power equipment, leaving no room for supplemental state laws (no field preemption),
  • enforcement of the state law would not directly interfere with the full execution of the federal statute since a lawn mower can satisfy both laws' requirements (no direct conflict preemption) and
  • the state and federal laws have consistent purposes since both aim to promote energy efficiency (no indirect conflict preemption).

Therefore, this is the state's best argument for the continued validity of its law.

(Choice A) The commerce clause gives Congress the power to regulate local activities that, singly or in the aggregate, substantially impact interstate commerce. Although the use of lawn mowers is a local activity, their aggregated sales likely have a substantial impact on interstate commerce. As a result, they are within Congress's regulatory authority.

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment reserves to the states all powers that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government—including the police power to enact and enforce laws that protect the public's health, safety, and welfare. But there is no presumption that state laws prevail over federal laws.

📌 Educational Objective

The supremacy clause allows federal laws to expressly or impliedly preempt conflicting state laws. But there is a presumption against preemption that is only overcome when Congress clearly intended to supersede state laws.

📚 References
  • Gade v. Nat'l Solid Wastes Mgmt. Ass'n, 505 U.S. 88, 98 (1992) (explaining when federal law expressly or impliedly preempts state law).
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 234 (2019) (stating the tests used to determine preemption).

一项新的联邦法规要求，所有动力设备（包括割草机）都必须贴上能效标签，以便购买者在购买此类设备时能够做出明智的选择。该法规并未明示优先于州法律适用。

假设没有其他联邦法规或行政法规涉及动力设备的能效问题。

为维持其法律的持续有效性，该州可以提出的最佳论点是以下哪一项？

zh-choices.A: 国会不能优先适用州法律，因为使用此类设备纯属地方性活动，因此超出了《商业条款》赋予国会的监管权力。
zh-choices.B: 该州法律不受联邦法规的影响，因为国会并未明示禁止州法律要求动力设备达到特定的燃油效率水平。
zh-choices.C: 该州法律的目的与联邦法规的目的相一致，执行该州法律不会妨碍联邦法规的全面执行，且没有证据表明国会有意阻止各州就此主题制定补充性法律。
zh-choices.D: 存在一个非常强的推定，即在通常属于州警察权范围内的事项上，特定的州法律优先于更宽泛的联邦法规，因为《第十修正案》将影响公共健康、福利和安全事务的主要权力保留给了各州。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 宪法考点解析

联邦优先权 (Preemption)
⚖️ 核心考点：至上条款

本题考查的是美国宪法第六条的至上条款 (Supremacy Clause)。当联邦法律与州法律发生冲突时，联邦法律优先。

联邦优先适用 (Preemption) 的三种形式：
  1. 明示优先 (Express Preemption)：国会明确说明禁止州立法。
  2. 领域优先 (Field Preemption)：联邦监管非常全面，不给州法留空间。
  3. 冲突优先 (Conflict Preemption)：
    • 无法同时遵守两者 (Physical Impossibility)。
    • 州法阻碍了联邦目标的实现 (Obstacle)。
✅ 正确答案解析 (选项 C)

本题要求找出州政府维护其法律有效性的最佳论点。

案情分析：

  • 州法：要求最低燃油效率（实质标准）。
  • 联邦法：要求贴能效标签（信息披露），且未明示优先于州法。

为什么 C 是最佳论点？

1
排除明示优先：题目已说明联邦法规没有明示优先条款。
2
排除领域优先：没有证据表明国会想独占“动力设备”的所有监管权。
3
排除冲突优先：这是关键。
• 制造商可以既制造高效率机器（满足州法），又贴上标签（满足联邦法）。
• 州法的目的（提高效率）与联邦法（通过标签促进选择）是一致的 (Consistent)，而非冲突。

因此，州政府最有力的反驳是：不存在任何形式的默示优先 (Implied Preemption)。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (商业条款)：
Commerce Clause。这是个很糟糕的论点。虽然割草是地方活动，但其销售属于州际贸易。根据 Wickard v. Filburn 原则，国会有权监管。州政府如果用这个理由，必输无疑。

选项 B (仅依赖未明示)：
这个论点太弱。仅仅因为国会没有“明示”禁止，并不意味着州法就安全了。州法仍可能因为“默示优先”（如冲突或领域独占）而被废止。

选项 D (第十修正案推定)：
10th Amendment。这是一个常见的陷阱。虽然有“反对优先适用的推定” (Presumption against preemption)，但这并不意味着州法在冲突时自动优先于联邦法。至上条款明确规定联邦法是最高法律。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

遇到 Preemption (优先权) 问题时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 找明示：题目有没有说 "Federal law expressly prohibits..."？
  2. 找冲突：能不能同时遵守两部法律？(本题可以)
  3. 找阻碍：州法是否让联邦目的落空？(本题没有，反而互补)

如果既无明示，又无冲突，且国会没打算独占该领域，州法律有效。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A fatal virus recently infected poultry in several nations. Some scientific evidence indicates that the virus can be transmitted from poultry to humans.
Poultry farming is a major industry in several U.S. states. In one such state, the legislature has enacted a law imposing a fee of two cents per bird on all poultry farming and processing operations in the state. The purpose of the fee is to pay for a state inspection system to ensure that no poultry raised or processed in the state is infected with the virus.
A company that has poultry processing plants both in the state and in other states has sued to challenge the fee.
Is the fee constitutional?

choices.A: No, because although it attaches only to intrastate activity, in the aggregate, the fee substantially affects interstate commerce.
choices.B: No, because it places an undue burden on interstate commerce in violation of the negative implications of the commerce clause.
choices.C: Yes, because it applies only to activities that take place wholly within the state, and it does not unduly burden interstate commerce.
choices.D: Yes, because it was enacted pursuant to the state's police power, which takes precedence over the negative implications of the commerce clause.

questions.explanation:
Dormant commerce clause
State regulation of interstate commerce prohibited unless:
Discriminatory law
Strict scrutiny
  • Law furthers legitimate interest and
  • no reasonable alternatives
Nondiscriminatory law
Undue burden test
  • Burden on commerce does not clearly exceed local benefit
State tax
Complete Auto test
  • Substantial nexus
  • fairly apportioned
  • nondiscriminatory and
  • fairly related to service/benefit
Other exceptions
  • Congressional approval
  • State = market participant
  • Subsidy
  • Traditional government function

The commerce clause gives Congress the power to regulate interstate commerce—ie, nearly all activities involving two or more states. This clause also carries a negative implication (ie, the dormant commerce clause) that prohibits states from discriminating against or unduly burdening interstate commerce. But a state tax that affects interstate commerce is not unduly burdensome if the tax is:

  • applied to a person or activity that has a substantial nexus with the state
  • fairly apportioned to avoid taxing activities performed in other states
  • not discriminatory against interstate commerce and
  • fairly related to services or benefits provided by the state.

Here, the state law imposes a fee (ie, tax) on all poultry farming and processing operations in the state. Although the fee only attaches to intrastate activity, in the aggregate, the fee likely has a substantial effect on interstate commerce (Choice A) But it does not unduly burden interstate commerce—and is therefore constitutional—because:

(Choice B) the entities taxed have poultry farming and processing operations in the state (substantial nexus)

the fee only applies to birds raised or processed in the state (fairly apportioned)

the fee applies to all poultry farming and processing operations in the state (nondiscriminatory) and

the fee appears reasonable compared to the poultry inspection system that the state will provide (fairly related) (Choice B).

(Choice D) The Tenth Amendment gives states all powers that are not expressly granted to the federal government by the Constitution—eg, police power to impose taxes on state activities. But pursuant to the supremacy clause, state police powers do not take precedence over other constitutional provisions, including the negative implications of the commerce clause.

📌 Educational Objective

A state tax that affects interstate commerce does not violate the dormant commerce clause if it is (1) applied to a person or activity that has a substantial nexus with the state, (2) fairly apportioned, (3) nondiscriminatory, and (4) fairly related to services or benefits provided by the state.

📚 References
  • Complete Auto Transit, Inc. v. Brady, 430 U.S. 274, 279 (1977) (setting forth the four-factor test for determining whether a state tax violates the commerce clause).
questions.zh-question:
一种致命病毒最近在几个国家感染了家禽。一些科学证据表明，该病毒可以从家禽传播给人类。

家禽养殖是美国几个州的主要产业。在其中一个州，立法机关颁布了一项法律，对州内所有的家禽养殖和加工业务征收每只家禽两美分的费用。该费用的目的是为一个州检查系统提供资金，以确保在该州饲养或加工的家禽没有感染该病毒。

一家在该州和其它州都设有家禽加工厂的公司提起诉讼，对该费用提出质疑。

该费用合宪吗？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为尽管该费用仅适用于州内活动，但总体而言，它对州际贸易产生了实质性影响。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为它对州际贸易构成了不当负担，违反了商业条款的负面含义。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为它仅适用于完全在州内进行的活动，且未对州际贸易构成不当负担。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为它是根据州的警察权颁布的，而警察权优先于商业条款的负面含义。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Dormant Commerce Clause

正确答案：C

本题的核心考点是休眠商业条款 (Dormant Commerce Clause) 下，州政府对州际贸易活动征税（或收费）的合宪性标准。

⚖️ 核心法律规则
Complete Auto Transit Test (四要素测试)
根据最高法院在 Complete Auto Transit v. Brady 案中的确立的标准，一项影响州际贸易的州税（或类似费用）若要合宪，必须同时满足以下四个条件：
  1. 实质性联系 (Substantial Nexus): 纳税人或活动与该州有实质联系。
  2. 公平分配 (Fair Apportionment): 税收必须公平分配，避免双重征税。
  3. 非歧视性 (Non-discrimination): 不得歧视州际贸易。
  4. 公平相关 (Fair Relationship): 税收与州提供的服务或福利合理相关。
🔍 案情分析

让我们将本案事实代入上述测试：

✔
实质性联系：该公司在该州设有家禽加工厂，并在该州开展业务，满足 Nexus 要求。
✔
公平分配：费用仅针对“在该州”饲养或加工的家禽征收。该州没有试图对该州以外发生的活动征税。
✔
非歧视性：费用适用于该州内所有的家禽养殖和加工业务，无论是本地公司还是跨州公司，一视同仁。
✔
公平相关：费用的目的是资助检查系统，这直接造福于该行业（确保家禽无病毒），因此费用与服务是相关的。

结论：该费用满足所有条件，没有对州际贸易造成不当负担 (Undue Burden)，因此是合宪的。

🚫 避坑指南 (为什么其他选项错)
陷阱 A：混淆了国会权力与州权力 选项 A 提到“实质性影响 (substantially affects)”。这是判断国会 (Congress) 是否有权根据商业条款进行立法的标准（Wickard v. Filburn）。

但在判断州 (State) 的法律是否违反休眠商业条款时，我们不看它是否有“实质影响”，而是看它是否构成“不当负担 (Undue Burden)”或“歧视”。
陷阱 D：警察权不是万能牌 虽然州拥有警察权 (Police Power) 来保护公众健康，但根据至上条款 (Supremacy Clause)，宪法（包括商业条款的负面含义）高于州法律。

如果州法违反了休眠商业条款（例如具有歧视性），即使它是基于警察权颁布的，也会被判违宪。因此，不能简单地说警察权“优先于”商业条款。
🎓 考试技巧

遇到涉及州税 (State Tax) 或州收费 (State Fee) 的题目时，直接套用 Complete Auto 四要素测试。只要该税收是非歧视的、公平分配的，并且与在该州的活动有关，通常都是合宪的。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute requires each insurance company that offers burglary insurance policies in the state to charge a uniform rate for such insurance to all of its customers residing within the same county in that state. So long as a company complies with this requirement, it is free to charge whatever rate the market will bear for its burglary insurance policies.
An insurance company located in the state files suit in federal district court against appropriate state officials to challenge this statute on constitutional grounds. The insurance company wishes to charge customers residing within the same county in the state rates for burglary insurance policies that will vary because they would be based on the specific nature of the customer's business, on its precise location, and on its past claims record.
How should the court rule in this suit?

choices.A: Abstain from ruling on the merits of this case until the state courts have had an opportunity to pass on the constitutionality of this state statute.
choices.B: Hold the statute constitutional, because the statute is a reasonable exercise of the state's police power.
choices.C: Hold the statute unconstitutional, because the statute deprives the insurance company of its liberty or property without due process of law.
choices.D: Hold the statute unconstitutional, because the statute imposes an undue burden on interstate commerce.

questions.explanation:
Under the Tenth Amendment, any power that the Constitution does not expressly grant to the federal government is reserved to the states. This includes the broad police power to enact and enforce laws that are reasonably related to protecting public health, safety, and welfare—eg, requiring insurers to charge uniform rates to residents is reasonably related to protecting their financial welfare (as seen here). But when exercising this power, states cannot violate other constitutional provisions like the due process and dormant commerce clauses.

The Fourteenth Amendment due process clause prohibits state deprivations of life, liberty, or property unless adequately justified. A deprivation impacting an ordinary right (eg, an economic right—as seen here) is justified if it satisfies mere rational basis scrutiny. Here, the statute satisfies this standard because it is reasonably related to the state's legitimate interest in protecting its citizens from varying insurance rates. As a result, the statute does not deprive the insurance company of due process of law (Choice C).

Additionally, the Article I dormant commerce clause prohibits states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. A nondiscriminatory law is unduly burdensome if its burden on interstate commerce clearly exceeds its local benefits. Here, the statute is nondiscriminatory since it applies to all insurance companies. And it is not unduly burdensome because there is no indication that it has any effect outside the state (Choice D). Therefore, the statute is a constitutional exercise of the state's police power.

(Choice A) A federal court should abstain from hearing a case that involves an unsettled issue of state law so that state courts can sort out the issue. But since this case concerns whether the statute violates the federal Constitution, the court need not abstain.

(Choice B) Hold the statute constitutional, because the statute is a reasonable exercise of the state's police power.

📌 Educational Objective

States possess the police power to enact and enforce laws that are reasonably related to protecting public health, safety, and welfare. But states cannot violate other constitutional provisions when exercising this power.

📚 References
  • O'Gorman & Young, Inc. v. Hartford Fire Ins. Co., 282 U.S. 251, 257–58 (1931) (holding that a state regulation of insurance rates is a reasonable exercise of the state's police power and does not violate the due process clause).
  • Kassel v. Consol. Freightways Corp., 450 U.S. 662, 669–70 (1981) (describing how a state acting pursuant to its police power can violate the dormant commerce clause).
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 379 (2019) (explaining that a state cannot violate other constitutional provisions when exercising its police powers).
questions.zh-question:
某州的一项法规要求，在该州提供入室犯法罪保险的每家保险公司，必须对居住在该州同一县内的所有客户就该保险收取统一的费率。只要公司遵守此要求，其可以自由地就其入室犯法罪保险收取市场能承受的任何费率。

位于该州的一家保险公司向联邦地区法院提起诉讼，控告相应的州政府官员，以该法规违反宪法为由对其提出质疑。该保险公司希望对居住在州内同一县的客户收取可变的入室犯法罪保险费率，因为费率将基于客户业务的具体性质、其精确位置以及其过往的索赔记录。

法院应如何裁决此案？

zh-choices.A: 对本案的实体问题不作裁决，直到州法院有机会就此州法规的合宪性作出裁决。
zh-choices.B: 裁定该法规合宪，因为该法规是州政府合理行使其警察权的结果。
zh-choices.C: 裁定该法规违宪，因为该法规未经正当法律程序剥夺了保险公司的自由或财产。
zh-choices.D: 裁定该法规违宪，因为该法规对州际贸易施加了不当负担。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations & Police Power

💡 核心考点：合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review) 当州政府行使警察权 (Police Power) 对商业或经济活动进行监管时，只要该法律与一个合法的政府利益 (Legitimate Government Interest) 存在合理的关联 (Rationally Related)，该法律通常就是合宪的。
✅ 为什么选 B？

本题考察的是州政府监管私营企业的权力边界。

1. 警察权 (Police Power)：
根据第十修正案 (10th Amendment)，各州拥有广泛的权力来制定法律以保护公众的健康、安全、道德和福利。保险业直接关系到公众的财务安全，因此属于州政府合法的监管范围。

2. 审查标准 (Standard of Review)：
本案涉及的是经济监管 (Economic Regulation)，而非基本权利 (Fundamental Rights) 或可疑分类 (Suspect Classification)。因此，法院适用最低级别的审查标准——合理基础审查 (Rational Basis Review)。

3. 逻辑推演：
州政府要求同一县内的保险费率统一，目的是防止价格歧视，保护消费者利益。这是一个合法的政府目的。该手段（统一费率）与该目的之间存在合理的关联。因此，该法规是警察权的合理行使，符合宪法。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 C：实质性正当程序 (Substantive Due Process) 自1937年以来，最高法院已不再使用“实质性正当程序”来废除经济法规（即推翻了 Lochner 时代的做法）。只要法规通过了合理基础审查，就不会被视为剥夺了公司的“自由或财产”。
选项 D：休眠商业条款 (Dormant Commerce Clause) 该法规并未歧视外州公司（它适用于所有在该州经营的公司），也没有对州际贸易造成“过度负担” (Undue Burden)。保险监管主要是地方性的，其本地利益通常超过对州际贸易的轻微影响。
选项 A：联邦法院回避 (Abstention) 普尔曼回避原则 (Pullman Abstention) 仅适用于州法律含义模糊不清 (Ambiguous) 且州法院的解释可能消除联邦宪法问题的情况。本题中法规含义明确，只是受到宪法挑战，因此联邦法院无需回避。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip) 在 MBE 宪法题中，如果看到州政府对商业、经济或社会福利进行监管，且不涉及种族、言论自由等基本权利：
1. 默认适用合理基础审查。
2. 法律几乎总是合宪的。
3. 寻找包含“Police Power”或“Rational Basis”字眼的选项。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The legislatures of several states entered into an agreement in which each state pledged to curb its pollution emissions. The agreement authorized a commission that contained a representative of each state to investigate how the states could reach their pollution emission goals and propose solutions for the states to adopt. The commission determined that each state needed to commit a fixed percentage of its energy consumption to clean energy sources, and each state enacted legislation that implemented the commission's suggestion. As a result, the states' demand for electricity produced by a company that uses coal-burning plants has significantly declined.
The company has filed suit against the commission in a federal district court, seeking a declaratory judgment that the states' agreement is unconstitutional.
Assume that no federal statute applies.
What action should the federal court take?

choices.A: Dismiss the suit without reaching the merits, because the Eleventh Amendment bars suits of this kind in federal court.
choices.B: Dismiss the suit without reaching the merits, because the suit presents a nonjusticiable political question.
choices.C: Invalidate the states' agreement, because the states failed to obtain congressional consent.
choices.D: Uphold the states' agreement, because the states validly entered into an interstate compact.

questions.explanation:
Congressional consent for interstate compacts
Required States' political power increased at federal government's expense—eg, states:
  • cede territory to each other
  • exercise powers they cannot exercise on own
Not required States do not encroach on federal government supremacy—eg, states:
  • enact reciprocal legislation for benefit of each state's residents (eg, state college tuition reciprocity)
  • form administrative body to study joint problems and make recommendations
  • create entity to operate transportation facility (eg, port authority)

States generally may enter into agreements with each other (ie, interstate compacts) without permission from the federal government.* However, the compact clause requires that states obtain Congress's consent for interstate compacts that increase the compacting states' political power at the expense of the federal government. This situation arises when the compact grants states or an administrative body powers that they could not exercise on their own.

Here, several states entered into an interstate compact to curb pollution emissions and created a commission that suggested that each state commit a fixed percentage of its energy consumption to clean energy sources. Each state did so. Since each state could have adopted energy guidelines without the commission's suggestion, the compact does not grant power to the states at the expense of the federal government. As a result, congressional consent was not required, and the federal court is likely to uphold the states' agreement (Choice C).

*The compact clause also permits states to enter into agreements with foreign governments if Congress consents.

(Choice A) The Eleventh Amendment generally bars suits in federal court against state governments. However, it does not prohibit suits against commissions created by interstate compacts (as seen here).

(Choice B) The political-question doctrine prevents federal courts from hearing the merits of suits that present issues that (1) are reserved to the executive or legislative branch or (2) lack judicially manageable standards for resolution—neither of which are seen here.

📌 Educational Objective

The compact clause requires states to obtain Congress's consent for agreements between the states (ie, interstate compacts) that increase the political power of the compacting states at the expense of the federal government.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 10, cl. 3 (compact clause).
  • U.S. Steel Corp. v. Multistate Tax Comm'n, 434 U.S. 452, 473–76 (1978) (holding that congressional consent was not required when an interstate compact granted powers that compacting states could exercise on their own).
  • 72 Am. Jur. 2d States, Territories, and Dependencies § 10 (2020) (explaining when congressional consent is required for an interstate compact).
questions.zh-question:
几个州的立法机关达成一项协议，其中每个州承诺控制其污染排放。该协议授权成立一个由各州代表组成的委员会，负责调查各州如何实现其污染排放目标，并提出供各州采纳的解决方案。该委员会确定，每个州都需要将其能源消耗的固定百分比用于清洁能源，并且每个州都颁布了实施该委员会建议的立法。结果，各州对一家使用燃煤电厂的公司所生产电力的需求大幅下降。

该公司已在联邦地区法院对该委员会提起诉讼，请求作出宣告性判决，认定该州际协议违宪。

假设没有联邦法规适用。

联邦法院应采取何种行动？

zh-choices.A: 驳回诉讼，不进行实质审理，因为《第十一修正案》(Eleventh Amendment) 禁止联邦法院审理此类诉讼。
zh-choices.B: 驳回诉讼，不进行实质审理，因为该诉讼提出了一个不可由法院裁决的政治问题。
zh-choices.C: 宣告州际协议无效，因为各州未能获得国会同意。
zh-choices.D: 维持州际协议的效力，因为各州有效订立了一项州际协定。

questions.zh-explanation:
核心考点：协定条款
The Compact Clause

本题考察的是美国宪法第一条第10款中的协定条款 (Compact Clause)。核心问题在于：州与州之间达成的协议，在什么情况下必须获得国会 (Congress) 的同意？

正确答案是 D。

法律规则解析

虽然宪法文本字面上规定“任何州未经国会同意，不得与他州缔结协定”，但最高法院 (Supreme Court) 对此进行了限缩解释。

关键判例规则 (U.S. Steel Corp. Test) 只有当州际协定增加了各州的政治权力，并以牺牲联邦政府的最高权力 (Federal Supremacy) 为代价时，才需要国会的同意。

不需要国会同意的情况：

  • 各州行使原本就拥有的权力（如本案中的环保立法）。
  • 成立仅具有咨询性质 (Advisory) 或建议权的行政机构。
  • 互惠立法（如大学学费互惠政策）。

本案案情分析

在本题中，各州成立的委员会 (Commission) 仅有权“调查”和“提出建议”。

  • 权力来源： 最终的法律效力来自于每个州各自颁布的立法，而不是委员会的直接命令。
  • 联邦利益： 这种合作没有侵犯联邦政府的权力，因为各州本身就有权监管能源消耗和环境污染。

因此，该协议并未以牺牲联邦利益为代价来扩张州权，不需要国会同意。该州际协定是有效的。

为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 A (第十一修正案)
虽然第十一修正案通常禁止在联邦法院起诉“州”，但最高法院已裁定，由州际协定设立的多州实体 (Multi-state entities) 通常不享有第十一修正案赋予的豁免权 (Sovereign Immunity)，除非该实体的结构和资金完全依赖于各州财政且被视为州的“手臂”。此外，本题考点在于协议的合宪性，而非程序性障碍。

选项 B (政治问题)
解释宪法条款（如协定条款）是否被违反，是法院的典型职责，存在司法上可管理的标准，不属于不可裁决的政治问题 (Nonjusticiable Political Question)。

选项 C (未获国会同意)
这是最强的干扰项。它错误地假设所有州际协定都必须获得国会同意。如前所述，只有侵犯联邦权力的协定才需要同意。

MBE 考试技巧

看到涉及 "Interstate Compact" (州际协定) 的题目时，请按以下步骤思考：

  1. 该协定是否建立了一个新的政治实体，其权力凌驾于各州之上？
  2. 该协定是否侵犯了联邦政府的专属领域（如外交、宣战）？

如果答案是“否”（例如仅是咨询委员会、互惠政策），则通常不需要国会同意，协定有效。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A man bought an antique car from a car dealer in State A. Under State A law, a person who buys from such a dealer acquires good title, even if the property was stolen from a previous owner. The man showed the car at an antique car show in State B. A woman recognized the car as having been stolen from her. Under State B law, a person whose property is stolen may reclaim it, even if the current possessor is an innocent purchaser.
The woman sued the man in a State B court to reclaim the car. In his defense, the man claimed that he had good title under the law of State A. Nevertheless, the State B court applied State B law, and the woman prevailed. The man did not appeal. The sheriff had the car returned to State B and gave the woman possession of the car.
Several months later, the woman moved to State A, bringing the car with her. The man brought a new suit against the woman in a State A court, claiming that the State B court in the prior suit should have applied the State A law, which protects innocent purchasers. The woman appeared and moved to dismiss the suit.
What should the State A court do?

choices.A: Apply State A law, because the car is currently located in State A.
choices.B: Apply the federal law on sale of goods, because the car has moved in interstate commerce.
choices.C: Dismiss the suit, because the State A court must give full faith and credit to the State B judgment.
choices.D: Remove the case to federal court, because the car has moved in interstate commerce, and therefore the case raises a federal question.

questions.explanation:
Full faith and credit clause
(duty to respect/enforce judgment by court in another state)
Jurisdiction
Personal jurisdiction over defendant & subject matter jurisdiction over claim?
No
→
No duty
↓
Yes
↓
Merits
Decision addresses substantive elements of claim or defense?
No
→
No duty
↓
Yes
↓
Final judgment
Court's decision settles rights of parties & disposes of all issues?
No
→
No duty
↓
Duty to respect & enforce

Under the Article IV full faith and credit clause, states have a duty to respect the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of other states. This requires state courts to recognize and enforce decisions rendered by a court in another state when:

  • that court had personal jurisdiction and subject-matter jurisdiction
  • the case was decided on its merits—ie, the substantive elements or grounds of the claim or defense
  • and
  • a final judgment was entered.

Here, the woman sued the man in a State B court to reclaim her car. And the State A court must give full faith and credit to the State B judgment since:

  • the man waived any right to challenge personal jurisdiction by appearing in the State B court and presenting a defense
  • state courts, including the State B court, have subject matter jurisdiction over virtually any case arising under federal or state law
  • the case was decided on its merits when the State B court applied State B's substantive law and ruled in the woman's favor and
  • the judgment became final when the man failed to appeal.

Therefore, the State A court should dismiss the man's suit.

(Choices A & B) The fact that the car is currently located in State A and has moved in interstate commerce is irrelevant in determining whether the State A court must give full faith and credit to the State B judgment.

(Choice D) Even if the car's movement in interstate commerce created a federal question, the state court cannot remove the case to federal court on its own initiative. Removal is only proper when the defendant requests it (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The full faith and credit clause requires a state court to recognize and enforce a decision by a court in another state when (1) that court had personal and subject matter jurisdiction, (2) the case was decided on its merits, and (3) a final judgment was entered.

📚 References
  • Baker v. Gen. Motors Corp., 522 U.S. 222, 231–33 (1998) (explaining when the full faith and credit clause applies to state court judgments).
  • V.L. v. E.L., 136 S. Ct. 1017, 1020–22 (2016) (holding that a state court cannot relitigate a case that has already been decided on its merits in a court of another state).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子在A州从一个汽车经销商处购买了一辆古董车。根据A州法律，从该经销商处购买的人可以获得有效所有权，即使该财产是从前任所有者处被盗的。该男子在B州的一场古董车展上展示了这辆车。一名女子认出这辆车是从她那里被盗的。根据B州法律，财产被盗的人可以收回其财产，即使目前的占有人是善意购买者。

该女子在B州法院对该男子提起诉讼，要求收回该车。该男子辩称，根据A州法律，他拥有该车的有效所有权。然而，B州法院适用了B州法律，该女子胜诉。该男子没有上诉。法警已将该车运回B州，并将该车的占有权交给了该女子。

几个月后，该女子搬到了A州，并带上了这辆车。该男子在A州法院对该女子提起了新的诉讼，声称在之前的诉讼中，B州法院本应适用保护善意购买者的A州法律。该女子出庭并请求驳回该诉讼。

A州法院应该怎么做？

zh-choices.A: 适用A州法律，因为该车目前位于A州。
zh-choices.B: 适用关于货物销售的联邦法律，因为该车已进入州际贸易。
zh-choices.C: 驳回该诉讼，因为A州法院必须对B州的判决给予充分的信任和尊重。
zh-choices.D: 将案件移送至联邦法院，因为该车已进入州际贸易，因此该案引发了一个联邦问题。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations / Constitutional Law
✅ 正确答案：选项 C 驳回该诉讼 (Dismiss the suit)。
因为A州法院必须根据宪法给予B州判决充分的信任和尊重。
⚖️ 核心法律依据
Full Faith and Credit Clause
(充分信任和尊重条款)

美国宪法第四条第一款规定，各州必须承认并执行其他州的司法判决。这实际上是将既判力 (Res Judicata) 原则扩展到了州际之间。

要触发该条款的保护，原判决必须满足三个条件：

1️⃣
管辖权 (Jurisdiction)： 原审法院（B州）必须拥有属人管辖权 (Personal Jurisdiction) 和事项管辖权 (Subject Matter Jurisdiction)。
2️⃣
实体审理 (On the Merits)： 判决必须是基于案件的实质内容作出的，而非仅仅因为程序问题（如管辖权不足）被驳回。
3️⃣
最终判决 (Final Judgment)： 案件必须已经终结，没有未决的上诉。
🔍 案情深度解析

在本案中，A州法院必须驳回男子的诉讼，理由如下：

  • 管辖权无争议： 男子在B州出庭并进行了抗辩，这构成了对B州属人管辖权的接受。
  • 已进行实体判决： B州法院根据B州法律审理了所有权归属，并判决女子胜诉。
  • 判决已生效： 男子败诉后没有上诉 (did not appeal)，因此B州的判决是最终判决。
⚠️ 关键考点：法律适用错误不影响判决效力

男子争辩的核心是“B州法院本应该适用A州法律”。即使B州法院真的犯了法律适用错误 (Choice of Law error)，这也不能成为在A州重新起诉的理由。

纠正法律错误的唯一途径是在B州法院系统中上诉。一旦判决成为最终判决，其他州（包括A州）就必须执行它，不得重新审查其实体问题。

❌ 干扰项排除
选项 A (适用A州法律) 错误。虽然车现在在A州，但所有权问题已经在B州得到了最终裁决。既判力原则 (Res Judicata) 禁止重新审理同一诉因。
选项 B (适用联邦法) 错误。这是一起关于动产所有权的私法纠纷，主要受州法管辖。虽然车辆跨州移动，但这并不自动触发联邦普通法 (Federal Common Law) 来取代州法判决。
选项 D (移送联邦法院) 错误。首先，仅仅因为涉及“州际贸易”并不一定构成联邦问题管辖权 (Federal Question Jurisdiction)。其次，移送 (Removal) 是被告的权利，法院通常不会主动移送。最重要的是，本案的核心是既判力问题，应直接驳回。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congressional hearings determined that the use of mechanical power hammers is very dangerous to the persons using them and to persons in the vicinity of the persons using them. As a result, Congress enacted a statute prohibiting the use of mechanical power hammers on all construction projects in the United States.
Subsequently, a study conducted by a private research firm concluded that nails driven by mechanical power hammers have longer-lasting joining power than hand-driven nails. After learning about this study, a city council enacted an amendment to its building safety code requiring the use of mechanical power hammers in the construction of all buildings intended for human habitation.
Is this amendment to the city's building safety code constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it conflicts with the provisions of the federal statute.
choices.B: No, because it was enacted subsequent to the federal statute.
choices.C: Yes, because the federal statute does not expressly indicate that it supersedes inconsistent state or local laws.
choices.D: Yes, because the long-term safety of human habitations justifies some additional risk to the people engaged in their construction.

questions.explanation:
Doctrine of preemption
Federal law supersedes state & municipal laws by:
Express preemption
  • Constitution says federal regulation is exclusive
  • OR
  • Federal law expressly prohibits state/municipal regulation
Implied preemption
Field preemption
  • Congress’s pervasive regulation shows intent to occupy entire field
Conflict preemption
  • Direct - nearly impossible to comply with both laws
  • OR
  • Indirect - state/municipal law frustrates federal law’s purpose

It is common for the federal government to regulate the same subject matter as states and/or municipalities because these governments share many of the same powers. But under the supremacy clause, federal law is the supreme law of the land. Therefore, a federal law can preempt (ie, supersede) conflicting state or municipal laws and render them void. One example is implied conflict preemption, which occurs when there is:

  • direct conflict - a state/municipal law conflicts with a federal law to such a degree that it is impossible (or nearly impossible) for a person or entity to comply with both laws or
  • indirect conflict - a state/municipal law frustrates the accomplishment of the federal law's purpose.

Here, the federal statute prohibits the use of mechanized hammers on all construction projects. But the city council amendment requires the use of such hammers on all construction projects for human habitation. These laws directly conflict since it is impossible for a company constructing human habitations in the city to comply with both laws. Therefore, the federal statute impliedly preempts the city council amendment and renders it unconstitutional.

(Choice B) In determining preemption, the timing of the laws is irrelevant. Therefore, it makes no difference whether the city council enacted the amendment before or after the federal statute.

(Choice C) Although the federal statute does not expressly state that it supersedes inconsistent state or local laws, it impliedly preempts them.

(Choice D) Federal laws always preempt inconsistent state and local laws—regardless of their justification.

📌 Educational Objective

Implied conflict preemption exists when (1) it is impossible to comply with a federal law and a conflicting state/municipal law (ie, direct conflict) or (2) a state/municipal law frustrates the accomplishment of a federal law's purpose (ie, indirect conflict).

📚 References
  • English v. Gen. Elec. Co., 496 U.S. 72, 79 (1990) (stating that federal law preempts state law when "it is impossible for a private party to comply with both state and federal requirements").
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 235 (2019) (explaining when federal and state laws conflict).
questions.zh-question:
国会听证会认定，使用机械动力锤对使用者及使用者附近的人员都非常危险。因此，国会颁布了一项法规，禁止在美国所有建筑项目中使用机械动力锤。

随后，一家私营研究公司进行的一项研究得出结论，由机械动力锤钉入的钉子比手动钉入的钉子具有更持久的连接力。在了解到这项研究后，一个市议会通过了其建筑安全法规的一项修正案，要求在所有旨在供人类居住的建筑物的建造中使用机械动力锤。

该市建筑安全法规的这项修正案是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为它与联邦法规的规定相冲突。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为它是在联邦法规之后颁布的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为联邦法规没有明确表示其将取代不一致的州或地方法律。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为人类居住建筑的长期安全，为从事其建造的人员带来一些额外风险是正当的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

宪法：联邦与州的关系 (Federal-State Relations)
⚖️ 核心法律原则：最高条款

本题考查的是美国宪法中的最高条款 (Supremacy Clause)，位于宪法第六条第二款。

规则：联邦法律是国家的最高法律。当有效的联邦法律与州或地方法律发生冲突时，联邦法律优先适用 (Preempts)，州法无效。
🔍 案情冲突分析

本案中存在典型的“物理上的不可能” (Physical Impossibility)：

联邦法律
🚫 禁止
使用动力锤
VS
市议会法规
⚠️ 强制
使用动力锤

建筑商不可能同时遵守这两条法律：你无法在“必须使用”某工具的同时又“禁止使用”它。

✅ 正确答案：选项 A

"No, because it conflicts with the provisions of the federal statute."

解析：

  • 这是默示冲突优先适用 (Implied Conflict Preemption) 的教科书式案例。
  • 当遵守州法和联邦法在物理上是不可能的 (physically impossible) 时，联邦法自动废止州法。
  • 不论州法的初衷多么良好（为了建筑更坚固），只要与联邦法直接冲突，即违宪。
❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 B (时间先后)：
"enacted subsequent to..."
错误点：在优先适用权 (Preemption) 问题上，时间顺序无关紧要。只要联邦法有效，它就优于任何时间颁布的州法。

选项 C (明示条款)：
"does not expressly indicate..."
错误点：优先适用分为“明示” (Express) 和“默示” (Implied)。即使国会没有写明“本法取代州法”，只要存在实际冲突 (Actual Conflict)，默示优先适用依然发生。

选项 D (正当理由)：
"justifies some additional risk..."
错误点：这是典型的政策性干扰项。法院在判定优先适用时，不进行“利益权衡” (Balancing Test)。一旦确定冲突，联邦法胜出，州法的立法目的（即使是为了公共安全）也无法挽救该法律。

💡 MBE 提分技巧

在处理 Preemption 题目时，按以下步骤思考：

  1. 找冲突：能不能同时遵守两部法律？
    • 如果不能（如本题）→ Direct Conflict (直接冲突) → 联邦法胜。
  2. 找阻碍：如果能同时遵守，州法是否阻碍了联邦目标的实现？
    • 如果是 → Obstacle Preemption (障碍优先适用) → 联邦法胜。
  3. 看领域：国会是否意图独占该领域？
    • 如果是 → Field Preemption (领域优先适用) → 联邦法胜。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law makes it a crime for an individual to intentionally provide false information on state tax forms when applying for employment.
A federal statute prohibits employers from hiring individuals who provide false Social Security numbers when applying for employment. The statute's purpose is to prevent individuals from assuming a false identity to obtain employment. A provision of the federal statute states that the statute expressly preempts state laws imposing civil or criminal punishments on employers who hire individuals who provide fraudulent Social Security numbers.
A man was charged in state court with violating the state law by intentionally providing a false Social Security number on his state tax withholding form when he applied for employment in the state. The man argued that the prosecution should not proceed because the federal statute preempts the state law.
Assume that no other federal statute applies.
How should the state court proceed with the case?

choices.A: Determine whether the man intentionally provided false information on his state tax form and, if so, find him guilty of violating the state law.
choices.B: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the case and dismiss it, because the federal statute expressly preempts the state law.
choices.C: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the case and dismiss it, because the federal statute impliedly preempts the state law.
choices.D: Refuse to adjudicate the merits of the case and dismiss it, because the federal statute expressly and impliedly preempts the state law.

questions.explanation:
Doctrine of preemption
Federal law supersedes state & municipal laws by:
Express preemption
  • Constitution says federal regulation is exclusive
  • OR
  • Federal law expressly prohibits state/municipal regulation
Implied preemption
Field preemption
  • Congress’s pervasive regulation shows intent to occupy entire field
Conflict preemption
  • Direct - nearly impossible to comply with both laws
  • OR
  • Indirect - state/municipal law frustrates federal law’s purpose

The supremacy clause renders a state law void and without effect when a federal law expressly or impliedly preempts it. Express preemption occurs when a federal law:

  • was enacted pursuant to a power exclusively reserved to the federal government by the U.S. Constitution (eg, power to declare war) or
  • explicitly prohibits state regulation.

The federal government shares power with state governments to regulate hiring practices within the respective state. And though the federal statute here expressly preempts state laws that punish employers, it does not mention applicants. As a result, the federal statute does not expressly preempt the state law (Choices B & D).

The federal statute also does not impliedly preempt the state law. Implied preemption occurs through:

  • field preemption – when Congress intended to completely occupy a particular field by legislating so thoroughly that it has left no room for supplementary state regulations
  • direct conflict preemption – when it is impossible or nearly impossible to comply with both federal and state law or
  • indirect conflict preemption – when the state law frustrates the purpose of the federal law.

Here, there is no field preemption since the federal statute punishes employers but leaves room for states to punish applicants. There is no direct conflict preemption because individuals can comply with both statutes. And there is no indirect conflict preemption since the state law furthers the federal statute's purpose of preventing individuals from assuming a false identity to obtain employment (Choices C & D).

Therefore, the state court should adjudicate the merits to determine whether the man intentionally provided false information on his state tax form and, if so, find him guilty.

📌 Educational Objective

Express preemption occurs when a federal law is enacted under an exclusive federal power or explicitly bars state regulation. Implied preemption occurs when there is no room for state regulation (field), it is nearly impossible to comply with both laws (direct conflict), or the state law frustrates the federal law's purpose (indirect conflict).

📚 References
  • Kansas v. Garcia, 140 S. Ct. 791, 804–07 (2020) (holding that a federal law regulating employment hiring practices does not expressly or impliedly preempt a state law criminalizing fraud when applying for employment).
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law § 234 (2020) (explaining the tests used to determine preemption).
questions.zh-question:
一项州法律规定，个人在申请就业时，于州税表格上故意提供虚假信息构成一项罪行。

一项联邦法规禁止雇主雇佣在申请就业时提供虚假社会安全号码的个人。该法规的目的是防止个人为获得就业而冒用虚假身份。该联邦法规的一项条款规定，该法规明示优先于（expressly preempts）对雇佣了提供欺诈性社会安全号码的个人的雇主施加民事或刑事处罚的州法律。

一名男子在州法院被指控违反了州法律，因为他在该州申请就业时，于其州预扣税表格上故意提供了虚假的社会安全号码。该男子辩称，由于联邦法规优先于州法律，因此检控不应继续进行。

假设没有其他联邦法规适用。

州法院应如何处理此案？

zh-choices.A: 裁定该男子是否在其州税表格上故意提供了虚假信息，如果是，则裁定他违反州法律的罪名成立。
zh-choices.B: 拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决并予以驳回，因为联邦法规明示优先于州法律。
zh-choices.C: 拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决并予以驳回，因为联邦法规默示优先于州法律。
zh-choices.D: 拒绝就案件的实体问题进行裁决并予以驳回，因为联邦法规明示和默示地优先于州法律。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations | Preemption
正确答案：A 州法院应裁定该男子是否故意提供虚假信息，如属实则定罪。联邦法律并未优先于（Preempt）该州法律。
核心法律原则：联邦优先权 (Preemption)

根据美国宪法《至上条款》（Supremacy Clause），当联邦法律与州法律发生冲突时，联邦法律优先。优先权分为两类：

1. 明示优先 (Express Preemption)
联邦法律文本中明确写明禁止州进行监管。
🔍 本题分析：联邦法规明确禁止的是对雇主的处罚。而本案被告是雇员/申请人。因此，明示优先条款不适用。
2. 默示优先 (Implied Preemption)
虽然没有明文规定，但通过以下方式体现：
  • 领域优先 (Field Preemption): 联邦监管如此全面，不给州留空间（如移民身份登记）。
  • 冲突优先 (Conflict Preemption):
    • 无法同时遵守两者；或
    • 州法律阻碍了联邦目标的实现。
🔍 本题分析：州法律惩罚欺诈行为，这实际上促进（而非阻碍）了联邦防止身份欺诈的目标。且雇佣法通常是州行使警察权（Police Power）的领域，非联邦独占。
逻辑图解
联邦法规
对象：雇主 (Employers)
禁止：雇佣假身份者
(未提及申请人)
州法律
对象：个人 (Individuals)
禁止：税表造假
(与联邦互补)

两者针对不同主体，互不冲突 → 无 Preemption

判例背景 (Case Reference)
Kansas v. Garcia (2020) 本题改编自美国最高法院2020年的真实判例。法院裁定，尽管联邦《移民改革与控制法案》(IRCA) 规范了就业资格验证，但它并不优先于州政府利用州税表上的信息来起诉身份盗窃或欺诈行为的权力。
MBE 解题技巧
  • 仔细阅读优先权条款的范围：如果条款说“禁止各州监管X”，不要自动推导为“禁止各州监管Y”。本题中 X=雇主，Y=雇员。
  • 寻找“阻碍”证据：如果州法律帮助实现了联邦法律的目的（如本题中的反欺诈），通常不存在冲突优先。
  • 区分主体：注意联邦法和州法分别惩罚的是谁。主体不同往往意味着可以并存。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Congress enacted a federal statute providing that any state may "require labeling to show the state or other geographic origin of citrus fruit that is imported into the receiving state."
Pursuant to the federal statute, a state that produced large quantities of citrus fruit enacted a law requiring all citrus fruit imported into the state to be stamped with a two-letter postal abbreviation signifying the state of the fruit's origin. The law did not impose any such requirement for citrus fruit grown within the state. When it adopted the law, the state legislature declared that its purpose was to reduce the risks of infection of local citrus crops by itinerant diseases that have been found to attack citrus fruit.
A national association of citrus growers has sued to have the state law declared unconstitutional. The association claims that the law is prohibited by the negative implications of the commerce clause of the Constitution.
Which of the following is the best argument in favor of the state's effort to have this lawsuit dismissed?

choices.A: Any burden on interstate commerce imposed by the state law is outweighed by a legitimate state interest.
choices.B: Congress has the authority to authorize specified state regulations that would otherwise be prohibited by the negative implications of the commerce clause, and it has done so in this situation.
choices.C: The state law does not discriminate against out-of-state citrus growers or producers.
choices.D: The state law furthers a legitimate state interest, the burden it imposes on interstate commerce is only incidental, and the state's interest cannot be satisfied by other means that are less burdensome to interstate commerce.

The negative implication of the commerce clause (ie, the dormant commerce clause) prohibits states from discriminating against or otherwise unduly burdening interstate commerce. As a result, states generally cannot favor in-state over out-of-state economic interests unless:

  • the state law furthers a legitimate, noneconomic state interest and
  • no reasonable, nondiscriminatory alternatives are available.

But this analysis is unnecessary—and states can engage in such discrimination—when Congress explicitly authorizes the state's conduct (or some other exception to the dormant commerce clause applies).

Here, the state law discriminates against interstate commerce by requiring citrus fruit imported into the state—but not citrus fruit grown within the state—to have a stamp showing its origin (Choice C). This law would ordinarily violate the dormant commerce clause since there are reasonable alternatives to prevent citrus fruit infections (eg, conducting safety inspections) (Choice D). But since Congress explicitly authorized states to require this labeling, this is the state's best argument to have the lawsuit dismissed.

(Choice A) Under the undue burden test, a state regulation is justified if its legitimate, local benefits exceed the burdens imposed on interstate commerce. But this test does not apply to discriminatory state regulations (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The dormant commerce clause generally prohibits states from discriminating against or unduly burdening interstate commerce. But states can do so when Congress has explicitly authorized that conduct.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 8 (commerce clause).
  • Ne. Bancorp, Inc. v. Bd. of Governors of Fed. Reserve Sys., 472 U.S. 159, 174 (1985) (explaining that states can discriminate against interstate commerce when Congress authorizes them to do so).
  • 15A Am. Jur. 2d Commerce § 27 (2019) (discussing congressional authorization to regulate interstate commerce).

美国国会颁布了一项联邦法规，规定任何州可以“要求标签标明进口到本州的柑橘类水果的州或其他地理来源地”。

根据该联邦法规，一个大量生产柑橘类水果的州颁布了一项法律，要求所有进口到该州的柑橘类水果都必须盖上标明其原产州的双字母邮政缩写。该法律并未对州内种植的柑橘类水果施加任何此类要求。在通过该法律时，州立法机构宣称其目的是为了降低本地柑橘作物被已发现会侵袭柑橘类水果的流行性疾病感染的风险。

一个全国性的柑橘种植者协会提起诉讼，要求宣布该州法律违宪。该协会声称，该法律被宪法中commerce clause（商业条款）的负面含义所禁止。

以下哪项是支持该州为驳回此诉讼所作努力的最佳论点？

zh-choices.A: 州法律对州际贸易造成的任何负担，都被一项合法的州利益所超越。
zh-choices.B: 国会有权授权特定的州法规，而这些法规在没有国会授权的情况下，本会被commerce clause（商业条款）的负面含义所禁止，并且国会在此案中已经这么做了。
zh-choices.C: 该州法律并未歧视州外的柑橘种植者或生产者。
zh-choices.D: 该州法律促进了一项合法的州利益，其对州际贸易施加的负担仅是附带性的，并且该州的利益无法通过对州际贸易负担较轻的其他方式来满足。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Federal-State Relations / Commerce Clause

核心考点：国会的授权

本题考察的是宪法中的一个关键例外原则：国会对州际贸易管制的授权 (Congressional Authorization)。

基本原则 (Dormant Commerce Clause):
通常情况下，如果国会保持沉默（未立法），Dormant Commerce Clause（休眠商业条款）禁止各州通过歧视州际贸易或对其造成过度负担的法律。
例外情况 (The Exception):
如果国会明确授权 (Explicitly Authorizes) 州政府进行某种管制，那么即使该州法律具有歧视性或阻碍了州际贸易，它也是合宪的。

这是因为宪法赋予国会管理州际贸易的权力是完全的 (Plenary Power)，国会可以将这种权力“下放”或“许可”给各州。

答案解析

正确答案：B

逻辑推理链条：

  1. 事实认定： 题目第一句明确指出“Congress enacted a federal statute...”（国会颁布了一项联邦法规），允许各州要求进口柑橘标明原产地。
  2. 州的行为： 该州随后颁布了法律，完全符合联邦法规的授权范围。
  3. 法律后果： 虽然该州法律只针对“进口”水果（表面上构成了对州际贸易的歧视），但因为有国会的尚方宝剑（明确授权），休眠商业条款的限制不再适用。

因此，该州最好的辩护理由就是：“国会让我们这么做的。”

为什么其他选项不是“最佳”？

选项 A & D (错误):
这两个选项试图使用利益平衡测试 (Balancing Test) 或 严格审查 (Strict Scrutiny)。
  • 如果国会没有立法，我们需要分析州法律是否为了合法的本地利益（如防疫）且没有更轻微的替代手段（如选项D所述）。
  • 但这在法庭上是一个很难证明的标准（通常歧视性法律会被判违宪）。
  • 相比之下，国会授权 (选项B) 是一个绝对的、不可反驳的防御理由，因此它是“最佳”论点。
选项 C (错误):
这是一个事实上的错误。该法律明确只要求“进口到该州”的水果贴标签，而不要求州内种植的水果贴标签。这在法律上构成了表面上的歧视 (Facially Discriminatory)。否认歧视的存在是一个非常弱的论点。
🎓 MBE 抢分技巧

在处理涉及 Commerce Clause 的题目时，请遵循以下步骤：

  1. 先看国会： 检查题干是否提到国会通过了相关法律？
    • 如果有联邦法律授权：州法律有效（本题情况）。
    • 如果有联邦法律禁止：州法律无效（Preemption/先占原则）。
  2. 若国会沉默： 才进入 Dormant Commerce Clause 的分析（区分是否歧视、是否过度负担）。

切记： 一旦看到 "Congress enacted..." 或 "Pursuant to federal statute..."，你的雷达就应该响起来：这通常意味着休眠商业条款的限制被解除了。
